intervention_label: Doxorubicin / mafosfamide (matrix-mediated chemoresistance mechanism)
model_system: two new patient-derived chondrosarcoma cell lines (one dedifferentiated, one grade III conventional central) in monolayer vs 3D chondrogenic pellet; nude-mouse transplantation of biopsies and one cell line
n_units: 10 biopsies collected; 1 transplanted biopsy and 1 injected cell line engrafted; 2 stable cell lines derived
control_arm: matched monolayer (2D) culture of the same lines
dose_and_schedule: low-dose mafosfamide or doxorubicin applied to 2D monolayer and 3D pellets
mechanism: Cartilaginous matrix laid down in 3D pellet culture slows diffusion of drug to the cell, so nuclear drug accumulation falls and the same concentration that kills in monolayer no longer does.
key_finding: The same cells were sensitive to conventional agents in monolayer and resistant to low-dose mafosfamide or doxorubicin once they had rebuilt a hyaline cartilage matrix in 3D pellets, with altered nuclear drug accumulation. Both lines carried IDH1, IDH2 and TP53 mutations with CDKN2A deletion and/or MDM2 amplification, matching the genotype spectrum of the patient's likely tumour.
caveats: Culture-format comparison rather than an in-vivo treatment arm; the engraftment yield of 1 in 10 biopsies is itself a statement about how hard this tumour is to model.

intervention_label: Doxorubicin / cisplatin with BH3 mimetic ABT-737 (apoptotic-block mechanism)
model_system: chondrosarcoma cell lines SW1353, CH2879, JJ012, OUMS27 plus two primary cultures; 3D pellet models
n_units: 4 cell lines + 2 primary cultures
control_arm: single-agent doxorubicin or cisplatin, and untreated cells
dose_and_schedule: doxorubicin or cisplatin dose-response, alone and combined with ABT-737
mechanism: Resistance sits downstream of drug delivery: BCL-2 family members hold the mitochondrial apoptotic gate shut, and a BH3 mimetic reopens it so that DNA damage is converted into cell death.
key_finding: Doxorubicin reached the nuclei of cells inside 3D pellets despite the cartilaginous matrix, and MDR pump activity was inconsistent across cultures, which undercuts both of the usual explanations. Adding ABT-737 to doxorubicin or cisplatin abolished viability with cytochrome C release and apoptosis.
caveats: No in-vivo arm, and the panel is dominated by conventional grade II-III lines rather than dedifferentiated ones. Directly contradicts the matrix-diffusion result in Monderer 2013 on the point of nuclear drug accumulation.

intervention_label: Doxorubicin with BCL-2/BCL-xL/XIAP or P-glycoprotein knockdown
exclusion_reason: In-vitro only, in two grade II conventional lines (JJ012, SW1353); the same anti-apoptotic mechanism is covered with a druggable BH3 mimetic and a matrix-relevant 3D model in van Oosterwijk 2012.

intervention_label: Doxorubicin and hypoxia-activated prodrug TH-302 in a hypoxic spheroid
model_system: HEMC-SS human chondrosarcoma multicellular tumour spheroids, day 7 (non-hypoxic) vs day 14/20 (hypoxic core)
n_units: spheroids assayed at three time points; replicate counts not stated in the abstract
control_arm: matched 2D monolayer culture of the same line, and day-7 spheroids as the non-hypoxic comparator
dose_and_schedule: doxorubicin and TH-302 dose-response on day-7 and day-14 spheroids
mechanism: Spheroid growth reproduces two features of the tumour at once: a glycosaminoglycan- and collagen-II-rich matrix that blocks drug penetration, and a pimonidazole-positive hypoxic core with VEGF secretion.
key_finding: Doxorubicin resistance rose with spheroid size (multicellular resistance index 5.0 at day 7 vs 18.3 at day 14), and doxorubicin autofluorescence confirmed it was not reaching the deep layers. The hypoxia-activated prodrug TH-302 moved the other way, working better on the larger hypoxic spheroids.
caveats: Single cell line, extraskeletal myxoid rather than conventional or dedifferentiated central chondrosarcoma, and no in-vivo arm.

intervention_label: HIF-2alpha inhibition plus chemotherapy
model_system: chondrosarcoma tumour xenograft mouse models plus weighted correlation network analysis of human chondrosarcoma biopsies
n_units: not stated per arm in the abstract
control_arm: vehicle and single-agent chemotherapy
dose_and_schedule: pharmacological HIF-2alpha inhibitor with chemotherapy; doses not stated in the abstract
mechanism: HIF-2alpha (EPAS1) sits upstream of the gene module that separates high-grade from low-grade chondrosarcoma, so blocking it removes the transcriptional programme for growth, invasion and metastasis rather than a single downstream effector.
key_finding: HIF-2alpha was elevated in high-grade biopsies and EPAS1 amplification tracked with poor prognosis; knocking it down cut tumour growth, local invasion and metastasis in xenografts. Pharmacological HIF-2alpha inhibition combined with chemotherapy was synergistic for apoptosis and removed the malignancy signature in mice.
caveats: No dedifferentiated-specific arm, and the inhibitor and dosing are not identified in the abstract, which limits how far the dose relevance can be judged.

intervention_label: Trabectedin (ET-743) with recombinant plasminogen-related protein B
exclusion_reason: The antiangiogenic partner (plasminogen-related protein B) never reached clinical development, so the combination is not an option that could be acted on; the low-vascularity argument it speaks to is carried by newer models with usable agents.

intervention_label: Mutant-IDH1 inhibition (AGI-5198) in chondrosarcoma lines
model_system: chondrosarcoma cell lines with endogenous IDH1 (n=3) or IDH2 (n=2) mutation, versus IDH wild-type lines
n_units: 5 IDH-mutant lines; treatment to 72 h and prolonged culture up to 20 passages
control_arm: IDH1/2 wild-type chondrosarcoma cell lines and vehicle
dose_and_schedule: AGI-5198 dose-response, 72 h and prolonged exposure up to 20 passages
mechanism: If mutant IDH were still driving the malignant phenotype, removing D-2-HG should reverse the epigenetic block it causes. It did not, which places the mutation upstream of an event the cell has already banked.
key_finding: AGI-5198 dropped D-2-HG by more than 90% but only one of three mutant IDH1 lines showed even a moderate viability decrease at 72 h, and proliferation and migration were unchanged out to 20 passages. Global gene expression, CpG island methylation and H3K4/K9/K27 trimethylation all stayed put.
caveats: In-vitro only, and the lines are conventional central chondrosarcoma rather than dedifferentiated, so this is the founder-event argument rather than a direct dedifferentiated-subtype result.

intervention_label: Mutant-IDH1 inhibition (AGI-5198), opposing result
model_system: JJ012 (IDH1 R132G) and HT1080 (IDH1 R132C) cell lines; C28 IDH wild-type chondrocytes
n_units: 3 cell lines; replicate counts not stated in the abstract
control_arm: IDH1 wild-type C28 chondrocytes and vehicle
dose_and_schedule: AGI-5198 dose-response in culture
mechanism: Same premise as Suijker: block the mutant enzyme, lose D-2-HG, lose the transformed phenotype.
key_finding: AGI-5198 lowered D-2-HG dose-dependently and cut colony formation and migration, interrupted cycling and induced apoptosis. D-2-HG was also detectable in plasma and urine of an IDH-mutant chondrosarcoma patient and fell after resection.
caveats: HT1080 is a fibrosarcoma line, not chondrosarcoma, which weakens half the panel; in-vitro only. Directly conflicts with Suijker 2015, and the ivosidenib clinical result in dedifferentiated disease sits closer to Suijker.

intervention_label: DS-1001b, selective mutant-IDH1 inhibitor (in-vivo evidence)
model_system: IDH1-mutant chondrosarcoma cell lines (conventional L835, JJ012) in vitro and in mouse xenografts
n_units: not stated per arm in the abstract
control_arm: vehicle; IDH1 wild-type comparators
dose_and_schedule: orally bioavailable DS-1001b; doses not stated in the abstract
mechanism: Mutant IDH1 inhibition demethylates H3K9me3 and restores SOX9 and CDKN1C, which pushes conventional cells back toward chondrocyte differentiation and arrests the cycle in the more dedifferentiated line.
key_finding: DS-1001b lowered 2-HG and impaired proliferation of IDH1-mutant chondrosarcoma cells in vitro and in vivo, with the transcriptional response splitting by cell type: differentiation in L835, cell-cycle arrest in JJ012.
caveats: The strongest in-vivo case for a mutant-IDH1 inhibitor in this histology, but the effect is growth impairment rather than regression, and JJ012 is treated here as the dedifferentiated surrogate on thin grounds.

intervention_label: Mutant IDH biology: glycogen dependency (founder-event context)
model_system: mutant Idh1 mice developing enchondromas, murine growth plate, and human mutant-IDH chondrosarcoma cells in vitro and in vivo
n_units: not stated per arm in the abstract
control_arm: IDH wild-type cells and wild-type murine growth plate
dose_and_schedule: pharmacologic blockade of glycogen utilisation; agent and dose not stated in the abstract
mechanism: Mutant IDH1 partners with HIF1alpha to divert carbon into glycogen, a deposit found only in mutant cells, so the metabolic consequence of the mutation persists as a dependency separate from D-2-HG-driven methylation.
key_finding: Glycogen deposition appeared exclusively in mutant cells from IDH-mutant chondrosarcomas and Idh1-mutant murine growth plates. Blocking glycogen utilisation changed tumour cell behaviour, downstream energetics and tumour burden both in vitro and in vivo.
caveats: The mouse model produces enchondroma, the benign precursor, not dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma; no clinical-grade glycogen-pathway agent exists.

intervention_label: CB-839 / metformin / phenformin / chloroquine (glutaminolysis)
model_system: 10 chondrosarcoma cell lines with and without endogenous IDH1/2 mutation; glutaminase IHC on 120 cartilage tumours
n_units: 10 cell lines; 120 tumour samples for IHC
control_arm: IDH wild-type chondrosarcoma lines; untreated cells
dose_and_schedule: CB-839, metformin, phenformin and chloroquine dose-response in culture
mechanism: Glutaminase feeds the TCA cycle when isocitrate handling is disturbed; the prediction was that IDH-mutant cells would be the sensitive ones.
key_finding: Glutaminase expression rose with tumour grade (p=0.001), highest in high-grade chondrosarcoma, and all four agents had activity — but sensitivity did not track IDH1/2 mutation status. Metformin and phenformin lowered mTOR activity, and metformin's effect on LC3B-II was reversed by chloroquine.
caveats: In-vitro only, no in-vivo arm. The grade association is the transferable part; the IDH-stratification hypothesis that motivated the glutaminase trials is not supported here.

intervention_label: Talazoparib alone and with temozolomide or radiation
model_system: chondrosarcoma cell lines with and without endogenous IDH1/IDH2 mutation, including lines carried long-term on a D-2-HG-normalising inhibitor
n_units: cell-line panel; counts not stated in the abstract
control_arm: IDH wild-type lines; single-agent temozolomide or radiation
dose_and_schedule: talazoparib dose-response, alone and combined with temozolomide or irradiation
mechanism: The IDH-mutant 'BRCAness' hypothesis holds that D-2-HG suppresses homologous recombination and creates PARP-inhibitor synthetic lethality, as it does in glioma and leukaemia models.
key_finding: Talazoparib sensitivity varied widely and did not sort by IDH mutation status, and long-term normalisation of D-2-HG did not create synthetic lethality. A subset of lines was impaired in PARylation capacity, homologous recombination and MGMT expression, and talazoparib synergised with temozolomide or radiation independently of mutant-IDH1 inhibition.
caveats: In-vitro only. It supports PARP-inhibitor combinations in chondrosarcoma while removing IDH status as the selection biomarker for them, which matters for how the olaparib-plus-ceralasertib trial would be entered.

intervention_label: Carbon-ion versus X-ray irradiation of chondrosarcoma lines
model_system: five human chondrosarcoma cell lines (CH2879, SW1353, JJ012, FS090, 105KC) in normoxia and chronic hypoxia
n_units: 5 cell lines; survival curves, gammaH2AX, Apo2.7, SA-beta-gal, whole-exome sequencing
control_arm: unirradiated cells; X-ray irradiation as the comparator for carbon ions; normoxic culture as comparator for hypoxia
dose_and_schedule: single-dose X-ray and carbon-ion irradiation, survival-curve dose range
mechanism: High-LET carbon ions produce clustered, hard-to-repair DNA lesions, so cell kill is less dependent on the repair capacity and cell-cycle position that make photons ineffective here.
key_finding: Carbon ions caused more DNA damage and more cell death than X-rays across the panel, though the magnitude varied by line. X-ray response split cleanly — apoptosis and senescence in CH2879, one or the other in SW1353 and JJ012, no death at all in FS090 and 105KC — with p21 tracking senescence. Chronic hypoxia did not increase radioresistance and made JJ012 more radiosensitive.
caveats: In-vitro only, and the hypoxia result cuts against the standard oxygen-enhancement-ratio argument for why carbon ions should be preferred in this histology.

intervention_label: Proton versus carbon-ion RBE across sarcoma cell lines
model_system: four human sarcoma lines (MG63 osteosarcoma, HT1080 fibrosarcoma, SW872 liposarcoma, SW1353 chondrosarcoma) and three normal-tissue lines
n_units: 7 cell lines under one standardised colony-formation protocol
control_arm: gamma-ray irradiation as the reference radiation
dose_and_schedule: gamma rays; proton beam at the centre of the spread-out Bragg peak; carbon ions at 54.4 keV/micrometre LET
mechanism: RBE is the number that converts a physical dose into a biological one; if it varies by cell type, the fixed 1.1 and 2.1 used in planning systems are averages rather than facts about a given tumour.
key_finding: Mean RBE was 1.08 +/- 0.11 for protons and 2.08 +/- 0.36 for carbon ions, close to the 1.1 and 2.13 used clinically. Between-line spread reached 34% for protons and 32% for carbon ions among the sarcoma lines, and up to 48% between two normal lines under carbon ions.
caveats: SW1353 is the only chondrosarcoma line and it is conventional grade II; the physical rationale for carbon over proton (roughly a doubling of biological effect) is quantified here, the histology-specific part is not.

intervention_label: Olaparib with X-ray, proton or carbon-ion irradiation
model_system: CH2879 grade III chondrosarcoma cell line
n_units: single cell line; clonogenic and proliferation assays
control_arm: irradiation without olaparib; unirradiated cells
dose_and_schedule: olaparib with single-dose X-ray, proton and carbon-ion irradiation
mechanism: PARP inhibition blocks single-strand break repair, so the clustered damage from particles is converted into lethal double-strand breaks the cell cannot resolve.
key_finding: Olaparib gave sensitiser enhancement ratios of roughly 1.3 with X-rays, 1.8 with protons and 1.5 with carbon ions on clonogenic assay. CH2879 carried mutations in RAD50, SMARCA2 and NBN, which the authors link to its baseline radiosensitivity.
caveats: Single cell line, in-vitro only, and no dedifferentiated model. The largest gain was with protons rather than carbon ions, which is not the ordering the clinical modality argument assumes.

intervention_label: Carbon ions with miR-34 mimic and rapamycin (cancer stem cell fraction)
model_system: CH-2879 high-grade chondrosarcoma cells, cancer-stem-cell and tumour-initiating assays
n_units: single cell line; replicate counts not stated in the abstract
control_arm: carbon-ion irradiation alone; untreated cells
dose_and_schedule: carbon-ion irradiation combined with miR-34 mimic and/or rapamycin
mechanism: A radioresistant stem-like fraction survives irradiation; mTOR inhibition raises FOXO3 and miR-34, which represses KLF4 and strips the stemness programme that lets those cells re-initiate the tumour.
key_finding: High-grade chondrosarcoma cultures contained a radioresistant cancer-stem-cell population that carbon ions alone did not clear, and the triple combination controlled it along with the stemness phenotype and tumour-initiating capacity.
caveats: Single conventional grade III line and no animal arm; the miR-34 mimic has no clinical route in sarcoma.

intervention_label: Carbon ions versus X-rays in a normal-cartilage 3D model (normal-tissue side)
journal: Int J Radiat Oncol Biol Phys
model_system: primary human articular chondrocytes from a healthy donor in a collagen scaffold under physioxia (3D), with 2D culture as reference
n_units: one healthy donor; survival, cell-death and senescence assays
control_arm: X-ray irradiation at the same dose; 2D culture as the reference format
dose_and_schedule: single dose of a monoenergetic carbon-ion beam at approximately 30 keV/micrometre LET, the entrance-channel value upstream of the spread-out Bragg peak
mechanism: Entrance-channel carbon ions cross healthy cartilage before the Bragg peak; senescence rather than death is the relevant injury endpoint in a tissue that does not turn over.
key_finding: In 2D the carbon-ion RBE was 2.6 with a two-fold increase in radiation-induced senescence, but in the 3D physioxic cartilage model carbon ions and X-rays induced senescence at comparable rates. Measuring RBE in monolayer may therefore misstate the normal-tissue cost of a carbon-ion plan.
caveats: Healthy donor cartilage, not tumour, and a single donor. Speaks to the joint-preservation side of an acetabular particle-therapy decision rather than to tumour control.

intervention_label: Radiotherapy and periosteal stripping before femoral fracture (bone-healing mechanism)
model_system: female Wistar retired-breeder rat femoral fracture with fixation, after radiotherapy and/or surgical periosteal stripping
n_units: 4 treatment groups (control, radiotherapy, surgery, combined) across 3 endpoints (21, 28, 35 days post-fracture)
control_arm: untreated fracture; surgery-alone and radiotherapy-alone arms
dose_and_schedule: radiotherapy first, periosteal stripping 3 weeks later, femoral fracture with fixation 3 weeks after that
mechanism: Irradiated bone loses the chondroid and osteoid production that callus formation depends on, so the fracture defaults to atrophic non-union regardless of the mechanical fixation.
key_finding: By 35 days controls had united, periosteum-stripped animals formed hypertrophic non-unions, and irradiated animals formed atrophic non-unions with histomorphometry showing absent chondroid and osteoid. Periosteal stripping added little; radiation alone was sufficient.
caveats: Normal rat bone with conventional photons and no tumour present, so it speaks to healing of the fractured acetabulum after radiotherapy rather than to tumour biology or drug delivery at that site.

intervention_label: B7-H3 (CD276) CAR T cells
model_system: xenograft models of osteosarcoma, Ewing sarcoma and medulloblastoma; antigen-density titration in vitro
n_units: multiple xenograft models; per-arm counts not stated in the abstract
control_arm: untransduced or control CAR T cells; low- versus high-antigen target cells
dose_and_schedule: single intravenous or locoregional CAR T-cell infusion depending on the model
mechanism: CAR engagement is a threshold phenomenon rather than a binary one: below a certain surface antigen count per cell the synapse does not trigger full effector function, which is what creates a therapeutic window against normal tissue that expresses B7-H3 at low level.
key_finding: B7-H3 CAR T cells regressed established solid tumours including osteosarcoma and Ewing sarcoma xenografts. Efficacy depended on high surface antigen density and was greatly diminished against low-expressing targets.
caveats: No chondrosarcoma model anywhere in the paper; the density-dependence result is the part that transfers, and it cuts against a tumour whose measured B7-H3 H-scores are the lowest in sarcoma.

intervention_label: Anti-B7-H3 CAR constructs, avidity versus antigen-density threshold
model_system: three clinical-candidate B7-H3 binders across tumoroid re-stimulation assays, BEHAV3D single-cell video microscopy, and in-vivo models
n_units: 3 binder constructs; per-arm animal counts not stated in the abstract
control_arm: comparison across the three binders of differing affinity
dose_and_schedule: repeated tumoroid re-stimulation; in-vivo CAR T infusion
mechanism: Cellular avidity, not monomeric affinity, sets the antigen-density floor at which a CAR triggers; higher-avidity constructs hold longer CD8 contacts with dim targets and keep expanding.
key_finding: Functional avidity predicted the B7-H3 density threshold for effector function, with the better constructs giving longer cumulative CD8 CAR-T/tumour contact times, more CAR-T expansion and sustained control. Lower checkpoint-receptor expression did not correlate with better anti-tumour function.
caveats: Paediatric neuroblastoma and related models, no sarcoma-of-bone arm. Relevant because it defines what would have to be engineered around for an antigen-dim tumour, not because it tested one.

intervention_label: DS-7300a (ifinatamab deruxtecan), B7-H3-directed DXd ADC
model_system: human cancer cell lines in vitro; cell-line xenograft and patient-derived xenograft mouse models; PK in cynomolgus monkey; toxicology in rat and monkey
n_units: multiple xenograft and PDX models; per-arm counts not stated in the abstract
control_arm: B7-H3-negative cancer cell lines and vehicle
dose_and_schedule: DS-7300a intravenous dosing in xenograft models; doses not stated in the abstract
mechanism: Antibody binding to B7-H3 internalises a cleavable DXd topoisomerase-I payload, which raises phospho-CHK1 and cleaved PARP in the target cell.
key_finding: DS-7300a inhibited growth of B7-H3-expressing lines but not B7-H3-negative ones, and produced antitumour activity in high-B7-H3 xenografts and PDX models of several tumour types. It was stable in circulation and tolerated in rats and monkeys.
caveats: Every efficacy model is explicitly high-B7-H3; there is no chondrosarcoma model and no low-expression efficacy arm, so this does not address the expression tier a chondrosarcoma would most likely sit at.

intervention_label: DXd-payload bystander killing (DS-8201a, mechanism read-across)
model_system: co-culture of antigen-positive and antigen-negative cells; mouse xenografts with mixed antigen-positive and antigen-negative tumours
n_units: co-culture and mixed-xenograft experiments; per-arm counts not stated in the abstract
control_arm: T-DM1, whose non-cleavable payload does not diffuse; antigen-negative tumours alone
dose_and_schedule: single intravenous ADC dose in xenograft models
mechanism: The released DXd payload is membrane-permeable, so it diffuses out of the antigen-positive cell it was delivered into and kills adjacent antigen-negative neighbours; the non-cleavable T-DM1 payload does not do this.
key_finding: DS-8201a killed antigen-negative cells in co-culture and in mixed xenografts, while T-DM1 did not. This is the mechanism by which a DXd ADC can act on a heterogeneous or low-expressing tumour rather than only on strongly positive cells.
caveats: HER2 breast/gastric models, a different antigen and a different tumour entirely; it is offered as the payload-class rationale for why a B7-H3 DXd ADC might not need uniform high antigen, not as evidence that it works in chondrosarcoma.

intervention_label: B7-H3 membranous expression across sarcoma subtypes (target-density measurement)
model_system: two-centre cohort of 133 pre-treatment human bone and soft-tissue sarcoma samples, centrally stained B7-H3 IHC with H-score
n_units: n=133 (103 soft-tissue, 30 bone sarcoma)
control_arm: cross-subtype comparison; four B7-H3-negative samples
dose_and_schedule: not applicable
mechanism: H-score separates positivity from density. Both the CAR and the ADC literature make efficacy a function of surface antigen per cell, so a 'percent positive' figure and an H-score are not interchangeable.
key_finding: B7-H3 was expressed in 97% of sarcomas, but chondrosarcoma had the lowest median H-score of any subtype (60) against 175 for osteosarcoma and 202.5 for pleomorphic liposarcoma. H-score rose with histological grade across subtypes and predicted event-free but not overall survival.
caveats: Human tissue survey, not a model system, and the chondrosarcoma subgroup within the 30 bone sarcomas is small with no dedifferentiated breakdown reported. The grade correlation leaves open that a dedifferentiated component scores higher than the subtype median.

intervention_label: Immune landscape of conventional versus dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma
model_system: human tumour cohort, IHC (CD3, CD8, CD68, CD163, PD-L1, CSF1R) plus RT-qPCR for immune checkpoints
n_units: n=76 (27 conventional, 49 dedifferentiated)
control_arm: conventional chondrosarcoma as the comparator for the dedifferentiated group
dose_and_schedule: not applicable
mechanism: The dominant immune population is macrophage, not lymphocyte, and the checkpoints that are transcribed (CSF1R, SIRPA alongside B7H3, TIM3, LAG3) are largely myeloid ones, so PD-L1 positivity marks an inflamed dedifferentiated component without being the switch that controls it.
key_finding: TAMs were the main immune population in both subtypes; a high CD68+/CD8+ ratio was an independent poor prognostic factor (p<0.01) and high CD68+ tracked with metastasis at diagnosis (p<0.05). PD-L1 protein was confined to dedifferentiated tumours (42.6%), and CSF1R was expressed by TAMs in 89.7% of dedifferentiated versus 62.9% of conventional cases.
caveats: Descriptive human-tissue study with no therapeutic arm, so the CSF1R nomination is a hypothesis. PubMed indexes the author names in scrambled form; the 2020 corrigendum (PMID 32274326) gives them as Richert I ... Dutour A, which is what is recorded here.

intervention_label: Selective T-cell versus CD163+ macrophage depletion (syngeneic model)
model_system: Swarm rat chondrosarcoma (SRC) syngeneic model plus IHC on human chondrosarcoma samples
n_units: not stated per arm in the abstract
control_arm: undepleted tumour-bearing rats
dose_and_schedule: selective immunodepletion of T lymphocytes or of CD163+ macrophages in tumour-bearing rats
mechanism: Causal rather than correlative: removing the two populations in opposite directions separates which one restrains the tumour and which one supports it.
key_finding: Depleting T lymphocytes accelerated tumour growth, while depleting CD163+ macrophages slowed it. Splenocytes from tumour-bearing rats showed 27% specific cytotoxicity against chondrosarcoma cells, falling to 11% after CD3 depletion, and in both human and rat tumours the immune infiltrate sat in the peritumoral area.
caveats: Rat chondrosarcoma rather than a dedifferentiated human model; the immunocompetent design is what makes it worth keeping despite that.

intervention_label: Membrane-bound IL-15-engineered TILs from chondrosarcoma (cytoTIL15)
model_system: TILs expanded from immune-excluded human chondrosarcoma biopsies; autologous 3D tumour spheroid killing assays; spatial profiling of the TME
n_units: not stated per patient in the abstract
control_arm: conventional IL-2-dependent TIL expansion
dose_and_schedule: regulatable membrane-bound IL-15 expression without exogenous IL-2
mechanism: Collagenous matrix and myeloid infiltration exclude lymphocytes to the tumour periphery; membrane-bound IL-15 lowers the TCR signalling threshold of TIL clonotypes so the same T cells infiltrate and kill.
key_finding: Spatial profiling put ubiquitous collagen and myeloid infiltration forward as the resistance mechanisms, with lymphocytes largely restricted to peripheral regions — which is also where a TIL harvest would have to sample. Engineered TILs expanded from paucicellular chondrosarcoma biopsies and killed autologous 3D tumour models without exogenous IL-2.
caveats: Ex-vivo and 3D-model endpoints only, no in-vivo efficacy arm, and the work is sponsored by the company developing the platform.

intervention_label: Immune classification of conventional chondrosarcoma (CyTOF multi-omics)
model_system: fresh human conventional chondrosarcoma tumours profiled by CyTOF, whole-exome sequencing and flow cytometry, with mechanistic follow-up
n_units: 98 fresh tumours collected; 22 fully profiled; 12 patients received PD-1 antibody
control_arm: cross-subtype comparison among the three immune phenotypes
dose_and_schedule: not applicable (retrospective PD-1 antibody exposure in 12 patients)
mechanism: IDH mutation raised chemokine levels and immune-cell infiltration in otherwise immune-inactivated tumours, which offers a route by which genotype rather than PD-L1 shapes who is infiltrated.
key_finding: Three immune phenotypes emerged: G-MDSC-dominant, immune-exhausted, and immune-desert. The immune-rich subtypes were characterised by IDH mutation and high grade, and all 3 of 12 PD-1-treated patients with disease control were retrospectively classified as immune-exhausted.
caveats: Conventional chondrosarcoma only, so it does not directly cover the dedifferentiated component; the 3-of-12 clinical correlation is retrospective and hypothesis-generating.

intervention_label: Mifamurtide (TLR4 agonist) with doxorubicin
model_system: CH2879/THP-1 3D co-culture spheroids and CH2879 murine xenograft
n_units: not stated per arm in the abstract
control_arm: doxorubicin alone; mifamurtide alone
dose_and_schedule: mifamurtide combined with doxorubicin; doses not stated in the abstract
mechanism: TAMs can reach half the tumour mass in chondrosarcoma and sit predominantly in an M2-like state; a TLR4 agonist repolarises them, and the chemosensitivity of the tumour compartment changes as a consequence.
key_finding: Mifamurtide increased the chemosensitivity of CH2879/THP-1 spheroids, and in the CH2879 xenograft the combination with doxorubicin improved antitumour efficacy while reducing intermediate-stage TAMs.
caveats: Conventional grade III line, no dedifferentiated model, and mifamurtide's approved indication is paediatric non-metastatic osteosarcoma, so the regulatory route in this setting is not established.

intervention_label: Palbociclib (CDK4/6 inhibition) in chondrosarcoma
model_system: human chondrosarcoma cell lines with CDK4 siRNA and palbociclib; intraosseous chondrosarcoma mouse model read out by bioluminescence
n_units: not stated per arm in the abstract
control_arm: scrambled siRNA and vehicle-treated mice
dose_and_schedule: palbociclib in vitro dose-response; in-vivo dosing not stated in the abstract
mechanism: CDK4 phosphorylates Rb to release the G1 restriction point; where CDKN2A is deleted, as it is in a large share of dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma, that brake is already gone and inhibiting CDK4 restores it pharmacologically.
key_finding: CDK4 was expressed in human chondrosarcoma samples and correlated with metastasis and worse prognosis; siRNA or palbociclib cut proliferation with reduced Rb phosphorylation, arrested cells in G1 and reduced migration and invasion. Palbociclib reduced tumour burden within bone in vivo.
caveats: A 2023 correction replaced a wrongly uploaded Fig. 5C image with conclusions unchanged (PMID 36803557). CDKN2A status of the lines is not reported, so the biomarker link to this patient's untested CDKN2A remains inferred.

intervention_label: pRb-pathway restoration: p16 overexpression and CDK4 knockdown
model_system: chondrosarcoma cell lines OUMS27, SW1353, CH2879 with CDKN2A/p16 overexpression vectors and shRNA against CDK4; qPCR and IHC on 34 fresh-frozen and 90 FFPE enchondroma and chondrosarcoma samples
n_units: 3 cell lines; 124 human tumour samples; IHC subset of 29 high-grade chondrosarcomas
control_arm: empty vector and non-targeting shRNA
dose_and_schedule: not applicable (genetic manipulation)
mechanism: Reintroducing p16 or removing CDK4 rebuilds the same G1 brake that CDKN2A deletion removes during progression, which tests whether the pathway is still load-bearing rather than merely altered.
key_finding: Both p16 overexpression and CDK4 knockdown inhibited chondrosarcoma cell growth in vitro, and pRb-pathway alterations tracked with progression from enchondroma to high-grade chondrosarcoma in the tissue series.
caveats: In-vitro genetic proof rather than drug testing, and predates the availability of CDK4/6 inhibitors; establishes that the pathway is functional, not that a given inhibitor works.
